title: PauLie: Fast Classification of Pauli Dynamical Lie Algebras
authors: Oxana Shaya, Konstantin Golovkin, Mainak Roy, Vincent Russo
abstract: The dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) governs the controllability, expressibility, and simulation complexity of a quantum system. Explicitly computing it has been a major computational bottleneck: brute-force Lie closure scales exponentially in the number of qubits $n$. Many applications, however, consult only the isomorphism type of the DLA. We introduce PauLie, an open-source framework that decides this isomorphism type for DLAs generated by arbitrary Pauli strings, building on the anticommutation-graph reduction of Aguilar et al. PauLie runs in $O(n|\mathcal{G}|\max(n,|\mathcal{G}|))$ time, where $|\mathcal{G}|$ is the number of generators, turning DLA classification into a routine preprocessing step. We demonstrate its use as a structural oracle for routing Lie-algebraic simulation and Cartan decomposition, diagnosing barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, and engineering universal Pauli string generator sets with optimal generation rate.
summary: This paper presents PauLie, a novel, efficient framework for classifying the isomorphism type of Dynamical Lie Algebras generated by Pauli strings. By utilizing graph-theoretic reduction on the anticommutation graph, it bypasses the exponential complexity of traditional Lie closure methods. This tool is vital for analyzing quantum control, understanding system symmetries, and diagnosing issues like barren plateaus in quantum algorithms.
main_problem: The primary challenge is efficiently determining the isomorphism type of the Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA) generated by arbitrary Pauli strings, as explicit computation scales exponentially with the number of qubits.
main_result: The authors introduce PauLie, an open-source framework that classifies the DLA isomorphism type in polynomial time, $O(n|G| \max(n, |G|))$.
method: The method uses a graph-theoretic reduction algorithm based on the anticommutation relations of the generators, systematically applying graph contractions to map the structure to a canonical graph (Type A or B).
model_or_system: The system involves quantum evolution governed by Hamiltonians that are sums of Pauli strings. The DLA dictates the system's controllability and expressibility.
key_observables: The canonical graph structure (Type A, B1, B2, B3) serves as the classification invariant, which determines the DLA's algebraic isomorphism type.
important_parameters: The complexity scales polynomially with the number of qubits ($n$) and the number of generators ($|G|$).
main_assumptions: The algorithm assumes the input is an arbitrary set of Pauli strings and relies on graph-theoretic properties derived from anticommutation relations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the contraction process on anticommutation graphs and show examples of canonical graph structures (e.g., Type B3) corresponding to specific DLA isomorphisms.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the graph-theoretic canonicalization procedure (Algorithm 1), analyzes the computational complexity, and demonstrates the framework's utility as a structural oracle for quantum simulation and diagnosing barren plateaus.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, polynomial-time tool to analyze the underlying algebraic structure of quantum dynamics generated by Pauli operators, which is critical for understanding the limitations and symmetries of variational quantum algorithms.

Figure 5. Class diagram of the PauLie classification pipeline. A PauliStringCollection holds a generator set of PauliStrings. Calling classify() on the collection instantiates a Canonicalizer and a Classification; for each connected component of the anticommutation graph, the Canonicalizer (Algorithm 1) builds a Morph that is added to the Classification. The Classification is stored as an attribute of the PauliStringCollection and assembles the per-component Morphs, as the vertices of the canonical graph, into the direct-sum decomposition of the DLA.
